name: surf-agent-skill
description: Autonomous web research for AI coding agents, on Brave Search and nothing else. The CLI runs the whole loop: an LLM (DeepSeek v4 Pro via OpenRouter) plans the queries, up to --sub-agents of them run at once against Brave — paced to your plan's real rate limit — and follow-ups enter a priority frontier as tree nodes that know their parent and depth, so later waves descend into the thin branches instead of re-searching wide. Two modes: surf-search-normal (one wave, fitted inside the agent's bash timeout) and surf-search-unlimit (as many waves as the question needs). No valid Brave key means exit 78 before anything runs — it never quietly answers from somewhere else. Also ships surf-plan-agent-skill (research-driven execution planning), `surf` interactive setup with free live key validation, and a Node library.

scripts.test: npm run test:syntax || exit 1; bad=''; for f in ./test/smoke.mjs ./test/brave.mjs; do echo ''; echo "== $f"; node "$f" || bad="$bad $f"; done; echo ''; npm run --silent test:adversarial || bad="$bad test:adversarial"; if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "GATE RED, failed:$bad"; exit 1; fi; echo 'GATE GREEN'; exit 0
scripts.test:syntax: for f in bin/*.mjs src/index.mjs src/env.mjs src/install/*.mjs src/lib/*.mjs src/lib/ai/*.mjs src/lib/providers/*.mjs src/lib/api/*.mjs src/plan/*.mjs src/validators/*.mjs; do node --check "$f" || exit 1; done && echo syntax-ok
scripts.test:adversarial: bad=''; n=0; for f in ./test/adversarial/*.mjs; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; n=$((n+1)); echo ''; echo "== $f"; node "$f" || bad="$bad $f"; done; if [ "$n" -eq 0 ]; then echo 'no adversarial suite found under test/adversarial/'; exit 1; fi; if [ -n "$bad" ]; then echo "ADVERSARIAL RED, failed:$bad"; exit 1; fi; echo "adversarial GREEN ($n suites)"; exit 0
